page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core scaling. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression. However, its shared CPU allocation model introduces performance tradeoffs under sustained multi-core workloads, where stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the average tier. Memory performance is robust, with large-block read-only bandwidth reaching a strong top-25% tier at 197.78 GB/sec, though write bandwidth and small-block cached reads remain average. Text processing represents a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% on Geekbench.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density of 128 GB paired with a shared CPU model offers a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated multi-core compute execution. This makes the server well-suited for large-scale caching layers, in-memory databases, medium-sized Redis deployments, and lightweight LLM inference tasks using smaller models, where text generation speeds reach strong performance tiers.
